result:
The repo itself is tiny (133K, 42 loose objects) and `git status` already runs in ~0.4s, so there wasn't a real size/history problem to fix. I ran a couple of safe, non-destructive optimizations:

- `git gc` — repacked loose objects (no history/data was deleted)
- Enabled `core.fsmonitor` and `core.untrackedcache` — speeds up `status`/`diff` on Windows by caching filesystem state

I deliberately avoided aggressive/destructive options (`gc --aggressive --prune=now`, reflog expiry, shallow/history rewrites) since none were warranted here and they carry data-loss risk for no real benefit on a repo this small. If things still feel slow, it's more likely antivirus scanning `.git` on Windows — let me know if you want me to check that instead.
